title: Parameter table for the pathway map of the reasoning library
note: Facts only. Tags: M measured on this PC in the owner's repositories or session records; S taken from an outside study; G a guess. A number that only loosely relates to a parameter is a hint: the tag is G and the note says how it differs. Each parameter has a low, a high and a best value. The map draws values uniformly between low and high.

tags.M: Measured on this PC, in this owner's repositories or session records
tags.S: Taken from an outside study or the vendor's price list
tags.G: A guess. The note may cite a hint and say how it differs from the parameter

assumptions: Cost unit: one call by the cheap model (Sonnet) is 1. Calls are treated as equal in size inside a tier.
One period is 30 days and one piece of work is a fix-sized task of about ten cheap calls (brief section 12, R6).

Revision 2 (brief section 12): z_wrongstore removed; s_exact, s_similar, s_comp, s_part, ok_coverage_factor and fix_on_found added; c_carry, rho_retry, w_write, r_exact and h_harm re-tagged G (hints, not measurements); the k_fill source corrected.
m_opus is 2 and m_fable is 2 to 4 from the vendor price ratios supplied for this task (2026-11-12). Both are per-token ratios standing in for per-call ones.

Map refuter pass (2026-11-12, refute-map.md): m_opus re-tagged G (a per-token price standing in for a per-call setting); e_right re-tagged S (one of its three sources is an outside study); the notes of m_fable and u_similar now say where their best values sit.
Where a refuter corrected a first-round number, the corrected number is used.

parameters.source: No source. Hints: F3 s4 (tool errors are 2.2 % of calls); R10 s1.2 (windows with an edit or a failed check: 10.9 % of FixFlow tokens, 77.9 % of Clinic).
parameters.note: Hint only. Errors are 2.2 % of calls, and 11 to 78 % of tokens sit in windows with an edit or a failed check. Neither counts pieces of work.

parameters.source: No source. Hints: F6 s(iii) and R4 s1 (vendor scores, Sonnet 5.5 vs Opus 5.5); F6 s(i) (AgentBrew student alone 45.3 on Terminal-Bench 2.0).
parameters.note: Hint. On whole benchmarks Sonnet 5.5 fails about 29 % (Terminal-Bench 4.0) to 54 % (FrontierCode 1.1). Those are whole tasks, not one error or one failing check.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: R4 s1 (Clinic slice table, read again in this run).
parameters.note: Hint. Round-one review found a serious defect in 9 of 14 Opus-built slices and in 2 of the 4 Sonnet slices that have counts. These are slices, found by review.

parameters.source: R3 s1 (3 to 5 same-cause repeats in 48 to 50 fix commits on main; 95 % interval on 5 of 50 reaches 22 %); F5 H2 (outside study: 2.1 to 3.2 % of fixes rebuildable from past fixes).
parameters.note: 3 to 5 of 48 to 50 fix commits repeated an earlier cause (6 to 10 %). Hard fixes only, one repository, 64 days; includes same cause in a different file.

parameters.source: F2 s1 (X-05 F01 to F03: 17 to 45 % of bug fixes follow recurring fix patterns, secondary reads); F5 H2 (2.1 to 3.2 % rebuildable from past fixes in one project, unconfirmed summary).
parameters.note: Outside studies of many-contributor code put recurring fix patterns at 17 to 45 % of fixes. A one-project study found 2.1 to 3.2 %. Both were read second-hand. Best, 0.15, sits between them.

parameters.source: No source. Hints: F4 (one retrieved item scored best in ReasoningBank and SWE-Exp); F5 H2 (2.1 and 3.2 % of fixes buildable from one or several past fixes).
parameters.note: No study counts problems made of several stored parts. A one-project study found 2.1 % and 3.2 % of fixes buildable from one or several past fixes.

parameters.source: No source. Hints: F1 s5 (the diff check is the only route to problems the agent does not notice); F3 s4 (0 of 200 sampled search steps judged likely saved by an index).
parameters.note: No measurement. The design reaches silent problems only through a diff check, and a 200-step sample found no step an index would likely save. The range runs from almost nothing to no penalty.

parameters.source: No source. Brief section 12, R2 (entries come from strong-tier solves, and under the library the strong tier works only on what the cheap model failed).
parameters.note: No measurement. Entries exist for problems the cheap model failed, so a piece of work it gets right alone is less likely to have one. The top, 1, means no penalty.

parameters.source: F4 (APC: hit rate 2 % at 1 entry and 46 to 48 % at 100 entries; its 14.29 % is at the 20th percentile of queries, a cold-start curve over the query stream, not at 20 entries; AWM: most gain within about 40 examples; SWE-Exp: gains level off near 300). Corrected in revision 2 after verify-engine.md section 6.
parameters.note: Fitting the plan-caching study's two cache-size points (2 % at 1 entry, 46 % at 100, ceiling near 55 %) gives about 27 to 55 entries. Another study levelled off near 300. Both templated.

parameters.source: No source for a lookup. Hint: R8 s2 (forward replay over 154 changes, projected to 133 entries: some entry fired wrongly on 16 to 51 % of changes for the selective key types).
parameters.note: Hint. Replaying diff-keyed warnings forward over 154 changes, projected to 133 entries, some entry fired falsely on 16 to 51 % of changes. That is a push channel, not a lookup.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: R8 s2 (projections from per-entry false-fire rates).
parameters.note: Hint. Projected from replay fire rates, the false-fire chance reaches about 63 % of its top near 20 entries for loose keys and near 180 for selective keys.

parameters.source: No source. Hints: F1 s5 and s8 (pull-only design; compliance is self-reported and escalations without a lookup are undercounted).
parameters.note: No measured lookup rate exists. The design relies on the agent choosing to look up, and compliance is self-reported. The top of the range means every visible problem triggers a lookup.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: F6 s(ii) (agents that succeed 22 % of the time predict 77 %).
parameters.note: No measured rate. Some agents that succeeded 22 % of the time predicted 77 %, so asking only when in doubt is unreliable. Nothing signals these problems, so the rate is set low.

parameters.source: No source. Hints: F3 s7 (no measured number for one lookup turn exists); R1 s2 (one extra call per exploration run costs 11 to 16 % of tokens).
parameters.note: Hint. A pulled lookup is one extra model call, which is 1 by this map's unit. Low end: a script with no model turn. High end: a lookup plus a follow-up turn.

parameters.source: No source for a lookup's recall. Hints: F2 s1 (KS-O19 table: duplicate bug reports sharing no words, 33.6 % by title, 19.0 % by description, 5.1 % in both); F1 s1 (pilot target: recall at shown at least 60 %, a target not a result).
parameters.note: Hint. 5 to 34 % of duplicate bug reports share no words with their twin, so word-matching misses them. That is bug-report text, not stored fixes. The design's pilot target is 60 %.

parameters.source: No source for a chance. Hint: F2 s1 (BM25 scored 10.2 to 18.45 points lower on dissimilar duplicate bug reports than on similar ones).
parameters.note: Hint. Word-matching scored 10 to 18 points lower on dissimilar duplicate bug reports than on similar ones. That is a ranking score on bug reports, not a hit chance.

parameters.source: No source. Hints: F1 s3 (a lookup shows at most one lead and one candidate); F4 (one retrieved item beat several in ReasoningBank and SWE-Exp; Memento found more cases did not help).
parameters.note: No measurement. One lookup shows at most one lead and one candidate, and three outside studies did best with one retrieved item. Returning every part at once is therefore unlikely.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: F1 s3 (display cap of one lead and one candidate).
parameters.note: No measurement. One lookup shows at most two items, so returning some but not all parts is likelier than returning all. This and the previous value together stay at or under 1.

parameters.source: No source for a chance. Hints: F2 s2 (KS-C7: one error template with 2 to 3 causes scores a full match on the wrong cause); F4 (MeanCache test: 12.7 to 33 % false hits on queries that should all miss, search summary only).
parameters.note: Hint. Error templates here carry 2 to 3 causes, so a wrong-cause match scores full. Semantic caches gave 13 to 33 % false hits on queries that should miss (unconfirmed summary).

parameters.source: F1 s3, R9 s1.6 (3 of about 15 worked-example entries can return 'applies' without Docker, 6 of 15 with it; about 3 of 116 entry-bearing seed rows).
parameters.note: Counted in the design's seed: 3 of 15 worked-example entries carry a check usable without Docker, 6 of 15 with it, and about 3 of 116 across the whole seed.

parameters.source: F1 s1 (design estimate, labelled inferred: a native verify adds 2 to 3 turns).
parameters.note: Design estimate, not measured: a verify adds 2 to 3 extra turns. The check itself runs in 0.2 s with no tokens, so the low end is one call.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: F5 A1 (Xiong: agents copy stored records whose inputs resemble the new one, correlation near 1).
parameters.note: Hint. Agents tend to copy stored records that look like the current input (correlation near 1 in one study), so good entries are probably accepted. Not measured on coding work.

parameters.source: F5 C1 (ClashEval, arXiv 2404.10198: six top models adopted wrong retrieved content over a correct prior more than 60 % of the time).
parameters.note: Six top models took wrong retrieved content over their own correct answer more than 60 % of the time. Question answering with planted wrong values, not look-alike repair notes.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: F3 s1 (48 compactions in Clinic main sessions; what a compaction drops was never measured).
parameters.note: Hint. An entry stays in the window until a compaction or a handoff drops it. Clinic main sessions compacted 48 times. What compaction loses has not been measured here.

parameters.source: No measurement of carrying cost. Hint: D1 s2 (860 tokens x about 260 remaining calls / 306k tokens per call = 0.73, derived); answer size from KS-C9 (0.4 tokens per character on 2,904 results); 306k and 519 calls from F3 s1 and s7.
parameters.note: Hint, derived not measured: an 860-token answer, 306k tokens per slice call, 519 calls per slice, and an assumed 260 remaining calls (half the session).

parameters.source: F4 (Dynamic Cheatsheet: Game of 24 10 to 99, Equation Balancer 44.8 to 100, both one repeated template).
parameters.note: On a repeated template a stored solution fixed 89 of 90 failures (Game of 24). Net gain over baseline failures, on same-template puzzles. The design stores a diagnosis, not the whole fix.

parameters.source: F4 and F5 (net gain divided by baseline failures, my arithmetic: SWE-Exp 6.8 %, ReasoningBank 7.0 to 7.4 %, AgentBrew 11.5 to 20.8 %, Agent KB 11.4 %, AWM 15.7 %, ExpeL 15 to 32 %).
parameters.note: Net gain over baseline failures: 7 % (SWE-Exp, ReasoningBank), 12 to 21 % (AgentBrew, Agent KB), 16 to 32 % (AWM, ExpeL). These average over all retrievals, so a good fit should do better.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: F4 (ReasoningBank 49.7 at one item vs 44.4 at four; SWE-Exp 42.0 vs 39.0).
parameters.note: No study measures all parts of a composite. Two studies scored lower with more retrieved items, so this is set at or under the similar-entry value.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: same as q_comp.
parameters.note: No measurement. With only some parts the cheap model must work out the rest, so this is set below the all-parts value.

parameters.source: No source for this step on its own. Hints: F5 C1 (ClashEval: wrong content beat a correct prior over 60 % of the time; the same figure a_wrong cites); F5 C3 (MemCollab raw memory: HumanEval 42.7 to 34.1, GSM8K 73.0 to 56.6, MATH500 27.4 to 18.8).
parameters.note: Hint. The over-60 % figure is the one a_wrong cites, so one figure supports two steps. Raw stronger-model memory cut weaker models' scores by 4 to 31 %. Question answering, not repair.

parameters.source: No source. Hints: F3 s1 (FixFlow agent windows average about 12 calls); R9 s1.2 (median agent window 7 calls, p25 4).
parameters.note: Hint. FixFlow agent windows average about 12 calls (median 7). That is a whole agent run. The map sets one piece of work at about ten cheap calls (brief R6).

parameters.source: No source. Hint: W L01 C3a and C3b (a stored route would have cut 2 to 8 calls per wave-2 agent; one wave-1 agent spent about 8; with the route in its brief an agent recovered in 2 calls).
parameters.note: Hint. In one real case a stored route would have saved 2 to 8 calls per agent, of about 8 spent. On a ten-call task that is 0.2 to 0.8. One case only.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: W L05-4 (a stored fix would have saved a detour of a commit, its revert, stopped full runs and one Opus review; the entry showed the cause, not the fix, so adapting was needed).
parameters.note: Hint. In one case a stored fix would have saved a wrong commit, its revert and a review. It gave the cause, not the fix, so adapting still costs calls.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: same as s_similar; F4 (two outside studies scored lower with more retrieved items).
parameters.note: No measurement. Several parts must be read and joined, so the saving is set at or below the similar-entry value.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: same as s_comp.
parameters.note: No measurement. With only some parts the cheap model must work out the rest, so the saving is set below the all-parts value.

parameters.source: No source for a catch rate. Hints: R2 s1 (CI caught both mypy repeats; CI stayed green on both Expo pin failures); F2 s1 (SapFix: 131 of 165 patches passed tests, only 27 of 57 crashes fixed correctly).
parameters.note: Hint. CI caught both mypy repeats but passed both Expo pin failures. In SapFix, passing tests alone let wrong patches through. No catch rate was counted.

parameters.source: No source for a catch rate. Hint: R4 s1 (serious defect in 9 of 14 Opus-built slices at round-one review).
parameters.note: Hint. Opus-built slices still had a serious defect found by round-one review in 9 of 14. The record does not split what tests had already passed from what review found.

parameters.source: No source for the share per piece of work. Hints: R4 s1 (every slice in the Clinic table had an Opus review); V2 (a reviewer on every PR).
parameters.note: Measured per slice: every Clinic slice had an Opus review. A slice holds many pieces of work, so the share per gate pass is lower. Best value is a guess.

parameters.source: No source for a catch rate. Hints: HB s3.3 (19 serious findings at round one; at least 5 more later, made by the fixes); R4 s1.
parameters.note: Hint. Round one found 19 serious defects; at least 5 more appeared later, made by the fixes. What reviews missed was never counted, so no catch rate exists.

parameters.source: No source for review length. Hints: R9 s1.2 (reviewer as a fresh agent of 3 to 7 calls); D7 s2 (reviewer 3 to 5 turns).
parameters.note: Estimates only: a reviewer agent of 3 to 7 calls (R9) or 3 to 5 turns (D7). The length of an actual Opus review was not measured.

parameters.source: No source for one cheap retry. Hint: V2 table row R1 and HB s3.3 (Clinic: 64 % of reviews sent a slice back; 2.8 rounds per slice). R4 clinic-gates-out.txt read again in this run.
parameters.note: Hint. 64 % of Clinic reviews sent a whole slice back, so a round passes 36 % of the time. Slices, not pieces of work; first and later rounds mixed; fixes mostly Opus-led.

parameters.source: No source for a price. Hints: R9 s1.2 (a fresh agent's first call is about 66k tokens); R1 s3.4 (opening exploration is 55 to 61 % of subagent tokens).
parameters.note: Hint. A fresh agent starts at about 66k tokens, and 55 to 61 % of subagent tokens go on opening exploration. Neither prices one handoff in cheap calls.

parameters.source: No source for calls per attempt. Hint: R5 s2 (Opus slice sessions: median 388 calls; Sonnet 283; different work).
parameters.note: Hint. Calls per slice session: Opus median 388, Sonnet 283, on different work. No calls-per-attempt by tier exists. Set equal to the cheap attempt.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: F3 s3 (Fable mostly ran long root sessions: 1,158 root calls in November).
parameters.note: No measurement. Fable mostly ran long root sessions, not single attempts. Set equal to the cheap attempt, with the same wide range.

parameters.source: Vendor price list supplied for this task (2026-11-12); F6 s(iv) (Opus 5.5 is 2 x Sonnet 5.5 per token, new and re-read).
parameters.note: Per token, Opus costs 2 x Sonnet (price list). The setting is per call. Calls here averaged about 222,000 cache-read tokens for Opus and 440,000 for Sonnet, so per call it is nearer 1.

parameters.source: Vendor price list supplied for this task (2026-11-12); F6 s(iv) (Fable 5.2: 2 x Sonnet on re-read tokens, 4 x on new input and output).
parameters.note: Vendor price ratio: 2 x Sonnet on re-read tokens, 4 x on new input and output. Best, 3, weights a typical call by its cost mix; that arithmetic gives 3 to 3.3.

parameters.source: No source for the conditional chance. Hint: F6 s(iii) and R4 s1 (vendor FrontierCode 1.1: Opus 54.4, Sonnet 46.2; Terminal-Bench 4.0: Sonnet ahead).
parameters.note: Hint. From vendor scores: if Opus's failures sit inside Sonnet's, Opus fixes 15 % of Sonnet's failures; if independent, 54 %. The overlap is unknown.

parameters.source: No source. Hint: R4 s1 (20 of 48 fix commits on main carry a Fable trailer; no failure rate by model exists).
parameters.note: No measurement. Fable authored 20 of 48 fix commits on main, but no failure rate by model exists. After Opus fails what is left is harder, which pulls this down.

parameters.source: No entry was ever written, so no write rate exists. Hint: R9 s1.1 and R9-git.json (a keyword reading flags 22 of 50 fix commits as meeting the design's write rule; 3 of the 5 first fixes in repeat pairs did).
parameters.note: Hint. A crude keyword reading found 22 of 50 fix commits eligible under the write rule (44 %); 3 of 5 first fixes in repeat pairs were. The top, 1.0, stores every strong solve.

parameters.source: No source for a call count. Hint: R9 s1.2 (0.4 to 3.8 M tokens per strict entry, from measured contexts and guessed turn counts); F1 s1 (design says 7 to 14k tokens).
parameters.note: Hint. R9 priced one strict entry at 0.4 to 3.8 million tokens (about 2 to 15 calls at 250k) from measured contexts and guessed turns. The design says 7 to 14 thousand.

parameters.source: R2 s1 (first lesson wrong in 1 of 5 repeat pairs); D7 s3 W2 (5 of 8 seed examples had a check or history error); P-proponent line 27 (AgentBrew curator rejected 24 to 38 % of drafts).
parameters.note: First lessons were wrong in 1 of 5 repeat pairs, but 5 of 8 seed examples had an error before refuters found it. An outside study rejected 24 to 38 % of drafted notes.

parameters.source: No source for a chance. Hints: R9 s1.1 (50 of 233 non-merge commits on main are fixes); F1 s3 (about 128 open defects stay in the register); F3 s8 (183 minor findings with no status).
parameters.note: Hint. 50 of 233 commits on main were fixes, about 128 known defects sit open in the register, and 183 findings have no status. None counts escapes found against escapes never found.

parameters.source: R9 s1.4 (a fix in a main session at 430 to 544k per call, 10 to 30 calls; R9 marks it an estimate).
parameters.note: Estimate: a fix in a main session takes 10 to 30 calls (R9, itself a guess). The high end allows a production incident.

parameters.source: No source for a chance. Hints: W L09-4 (a correction reached two files; verdicts.txt:30 still carries 742 s); W L10-2 (a refuted line was rewritten and still stands); W L08-2 (the record still says "They can").
parameters.note: Hint. In three real cases a correction did not reach every stored copy: an old figure, a refuted line and a refuted claim all still stand. Three cases, no rate.

parameters.source: No source for a rate. Hints: R3 s1 (the fix's own lines stay in main: 47 of 50 keep half or more); R10 s1.5 (fix footprint unchanged: 61 % at 1 day, 13 % at 30 days); R6 (value half-life 2 to 11 months, unmeasured).
parameters.note: Hint. 3 of 50 fixes lost half their lines within about two months, yet 87 % of fix footprints changed within 30 days. One period is 30 days (brief R6).

parameters.source: No source for a count of pieces of work. Hints: R3 s1 and F3 s8 (FixFlow 233 non-merge commits in 64 days; Clinic 432 commits in 8 days); F2 s4 (20 hard encounters per 8 weeks).
parameters.note: Hint. About 110 commits per 30 days in FixFlow, about 1,600 at the Clinic's pace, and 20 hard encounters per 8 weeks. A piece of work is not a commit.

parameters.source: Run setting (map.json). Hints: R6 (mid-tier models arrive every 90 to 141 days; value half-life 2 to 11 months, unmeasured).
parameters.note: A chosen horizon, not an unknown, and not drawn in the ensemble. 12 periods of 30 days is one year; mid-tier models arrive every 3 to 5 months.
